title: Interruption-safe compact panels and legacy-browser fallback patterns for Console pages
creator: Lila Chen
description: Design and prototype a compact/condensed Console surface that remains interaction-safe when interrupted (toasts, rollouts, reflow from live cost updates) and gracefully degrades on legacy/older browsers. Focus pages: Dashboards (cost explorer panels), Rollouts list/modals, and tabular traces. Deliver final specs, responsive tokens, and a small QA checklist for engineering handoff.
acceptance_criteria: Three responsive breakpoints documented (<=480px, 481-1024px, >1024px) with explicit collapse rules for cost table columns and chart legend behavior
Panel interruption flows: expanding a rollout row while a live-cost refresh occurs must not re-order focus or dismiss the expansion; documented keyboard/mouse flows
Modal stacking parity across tested browsers (Chrome 110+, Safari 16+, Firefox 113+, Chromium-based Edge older builds) with fallback CSS for missing features
Charts have a canvas -> SVG fallback for Safari WebGL rendering anomalies at small widths
Design tokens and CSS isolation recommendations included (containment, will-change guidance) to avoid jank on medium devices
A small cross-browser QA checklist and 6 annotated Figma frames are attached and reviewed by Eng and PM
notes: 2025-10-28: Kickoff with PM & Eng. Scope trimmed to three high-traffic surfaces to meet cycle: Cost Explorer dashboard cards, Rollouts table + details modal, and Admin traces table.
2025-10-30: Spike — prototype built in Figma with 'compact' density token set. Early discovery: chart canvas redraws cause scroll jitter in Safari on macOS when under 720px width.

2025-11-03: Trade-off discussion: prefer CSS containment + transform layering to avoid aggressive use of will-change which can exacerbate memory on low-end devices. Agreed to document guidance rather than global token change.

2025-11-05: Design review with Engineering (Ryan Patel) and PM (Aisha Patel). Engineering requested explicit fallbacks for PointerEvent vs mouse events and a non-Canvas fallback for small-chart micro-interactions.
2025-11-07: Accessibility review: ensure modals do not steal focus during live-updates — added requirement for aria-live regions to be polite and for announcements to be throttled.

2025-11-10: Prototype tested on BrowserStack sessions (iOS Safari 15, Safari 16, Firefox 102, Edge 18). Found Edge 18 has issues with position:sticky inside overflow containers; fallback uses a small JS shim described in implementation notes.
2025-11-12: Prepared final spec pages and QA checklist. Engineering PR reference and next steps noted below. Planning handoff meeting scheduled for 2025-11-13.
decisions: Use three explicit responsive breakpoints with deterministic column hide priority (action > status > created_at > id) instead of fluid collapse to reduce layout thrash
Provide canvas->SVG fallback for charts under 360px width due to Safari redraw anomalies; charts should default to static / simplified sparklines on very small devices
Mitigate sticky/overflow issues by avoiding nested overflow containers for important sticky headers; provide JS shim and fallback styles for legacy Edge where needed
Introduce 'interruption-safe' microflow: live-update signals must be queued with a 400ms debounce when a panel is expanded or modal open to avoid focus jank
open_issues: Confirm telemetry metric for 'layout-jank' to validate improvement after implementation
Decide on default animation curve for compact transition (ease-out vs cubic-bezier) after perf benchmarks
Front-end test coverage for pointer-event fallbacks; Eng to propose test plan

2025-11-02 Ryan Patel (Eng): flagged potential memory regression on low-end devices if will-change overused; recommended scoped containment and removal after transition
2025-11-04 Aisha Patel (PM): please ensure cost explorer export CSV still contains all columns even if hidden in UI (export uses full dataset)
2025-11-06 Accessibility Team: modal focus trap verified; requested aria-describedby for live update status messages
2025-11-11 Marco Alvarez: attached prototype build; engineering to start with Rollouts table then cost dashboard after canary
handoff_checklist: Deliver Figma frames + redlines for CSS variables (spacing, type scale, breakpoints)
Documented interaction flows for expand/collapse, live-update interruption, and keyboard navigation
QA checklist with BrowserStack permutations and known fallbacks
List of required small runtime flags and suggested rollout plan (canary -> 10% -> 50% -> global)
final_note: This ticket bundles UI patterns and explicit fallbacks so Engineering can roll out compact-mode with low risk of cross-browser regressions. Aim for a conservative rollout with telemetry to verify reduced layout jank and no accessibility regressions.
